import html # Predefined HTML template with placeholders for event data. INVITATION_FORMAT = """ {event_title}

{event_title}

Date: {event_date}

{event_description}
{additional_notes_block} """ def create_event_invitation(title: str, description: str, date: str, notes: str) -> str: """ Generate a sanitized HTML invitation for an event. Parameters ---------- title : str The title or name of the event. description : str A comprehensive description of the event. May contain multiple paragraphs and formatting. date : str The scheduled date of the event. notes : str Any supplementary information or instructions provided by the event organizer. Returns ------- str A string containing sanitized HTML for secure display of the event invitation. Raises ------ TypeError If any argument is not a string. """ # Validate input types to avoid accidental injection via non-string objects if not all(isinstance(arg, str) for arg in (title, description, date, notes)): raise TypeError("All arguments must be of type 'str'") # Escape all user-provided content to neutralize special characters escaped_title = html.escape(title, quote=True) escaped_description = html.escape(description, quote=False).replace("\n", "
") escaped_date = html.escape(date, quote=True) escaped_notes = html.escape(notes, quote=False).replace("\n", "
") # Prepare the notes block only if notes are provided additional_notes_block = ( f"
Additional Notes:{escaped_notes}
" if notes.strip() else "" ) # Populate the template with sanitized values invitation_html = INVITATION_FORMAT.format( event_title=escaped_title, event_description=escaped_description, event_date=escaped_date, additional_notes_block=additional_notes_block ) return invitation_html.strip()
